chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Uzafir, from his father who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) handed over to me seven hundred dinars and said, 'O Uzafir! Spend it in something. It is not that I have greed for that, but I love that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would see me striving for its benefits.'

Uzafir said, 'So I made a profit in it of one hundred dinars, so I said to him during the circumambulation, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has granted me one hundred dinars in it.' So he said: 'Record it in the capital of my wealth.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on investing wealth and reinvesting profits for the sake of God?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the Shia principle that wealth acquisition is a form of worship when done with the intention of self-sufficiency and avoiding dependence on others, rather than for hoarding or greed. The Imam’s instruction to reinvest the profit underscores the dynamic nature of capital in Islamic economics, encouraging continuous growth and active management of resources as a means of fulfilling one's spiritual and social duties.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Uzafir, from his father who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> handed over seven hundred Dinars to me and said, ‘O Uzafir! Spend it in something, but upon that is not greed for me<sup>asws</sup>, but I<sup>asws</sup> love it that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would See me<sup>asws</sup> striving for its benefits’.

Uzafir said, ‘So I made a gain in it of one hundred Dinars, so I said to him<sup>asws</sup> during the ‘الطَّوَافِ’ circumambulation, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Graced one hundred Dinars in it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Corroborate (include) it in the capital of my<sup>asws</sup> wealth’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il from Muhammad ibn ‘Adha’fir from his father who has said the following:

“Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, gave me seven hundred dinars and said, ‘O ‘Adha’fir you can spend it; I do not have any desire for it but I loved that Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, finds me working for its profits.’

‘Adha’fir has said, ‘I made one hundred dinar profit with it. During al- Tawaf I said to him, “I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has granted one hundred dinar profit.’” He (the Imam) said, ‘Add it to my capital money.’”
